description: A persistent broadcast server association sends periodic broadcast server (mode 5) packets that can be received by multiple clients.
note: The description is from section 3. The fields are the header of Figure 8, the same in the five message files of this interface.

values.1: last minute of the day has 61 seconds
values.2: last minute of the day has 59 seconds

leap_indicator.description: 2-bit integer warning of an impending leap second to be inserted or deleted in the last minute of the current month.

version_number.description: 3-bit integer representing the NTP version number, currently 4.

mode.note: Values 0 (reserved) and 7 (reserved for private use) have no label.

values.1: primary server (e.g., equipped with a GPS receiver)

stratum.note: Values 2 to 15 are secondary server (via NTP) and decode to the number: a label names one value, not a range. Values 17 to 255 are reserved.

poll.description: 8-bit signed integer representing the maximum interval between successive messages, in log2 seconds.
poll.note: The interval is 2^poll seconds: 6 is 64 s.

precision.description: 8-bit signed integer representing the precision of the system clock, in log2 seconds.
precision.note: The precision is 2^precision seconds: -18 is about one microsecond.

root_delay.description: Total round-trip delay to the reference clock, in NTP short format.
root_delay.note: NTP short format (section 6, Figure 3): a 16-bit unsigned seconds field and a 16-bit fraction field, read here as one 32-bit integer scaled by 2^-16, which is exact.

root_dispersion.description: Total dispersion to the reference clock, in NTP short format.
root_dispersion.note: NTP short format (section 6, Figure 3): a 16-bit unsigned seconds field and a 16-bit fraction field, read here as one 32-bit integer scaled by 2^-16, which is exact.

reference_id.description: 32-bit code identifying the particular server or reference clock.
reference_id.note: The interpretation depends on the value in the stratum field, which the format cannot express, so the four octets are given as hex. At stratum 0 they are a four-character ASCII kiss code (section 7.4, Figure 13) and at stratum 1 the ASCII identifier of the reference clock (Figure 12): 47505300 is GPS. Above stratum 1 they are the server's IPv4 address, or the first four octets of the MD5 hash of its IPv6 address: c0000201 is 192.0.2.1.

reference_timestamp_seconds.description: Time when the system clock was last set or corrected, in NTP timestamp format.
reference_timestamp_seconds.note: The Seconds half of the NTP timestamp format (section 6, Figure 3): seconds since 0 h 1 January 1900 UTC. Subtract 2208988800 for Unix time. The count wraps in 2036; the era is not in the packet.

reference_timestamp_fraction.description: Time when the system clock was last set or corrected, in NTP timestamp format.
reference_timestamp_fraction.note: The Fraction half of the NTP timestamp format (section 6, Figure 3), scaled by 2^-32, which is exact. Add it to the seconds field.

origin_timestamp_seconds.description: Time at the client when the request departed for the server, in NTP timestamp format.
origin_timestamp_seconds.note: The Seconds half of the NTP timestamp format (section 6, Figure 3): seconds since 0 h 1 January 1900 UTC. Subtract 2208988800 for Unix time. The count wraps in 2036; the era is not in the packet.

origin_timestamp_fraction.description: Time at the client when the request departed for the server, in NTP timestamp format.
origin_timestamp_fraction.note: The Fraction half of the NTP timestamp format (section 6, Figure 3), scaled by 2^-32, which is exact. Add it to the seconds field.

receive_timestamp_seconds.description: Time at the server when the request arrived from the client, in NTP timestamp format.
receive_timestamp_seconds.note: The Seconds half of the NTP timestamp format (section 6, Figure 3): seconds since 0 h 1 January 1900 UTC. Subtract 2208988800 for Unix time. The count wraps in 2036; the era is not in the packet.

receive_timestamp_fraction.description: Time at the server when the request arrived from the client, in NTP timestamp format.
receive_timestamp_fraction.note: The Fraction half of the NTP timestamp format (section 6, Figure 3), scaled by 2^-32, which is exact. Add it to the seconds field.

transmit_timestamp_seconds.description: Time at the server when the response left for the client, in NTP timestamp format.
transmit_timestamp_seconds.note: The Seconds half of the NTP timestamp format (section 6, Figure 3): seconds since 0 h 1 January 1900 UTC. Subtract 2208988800 for Unix time. The count wraps in 2036; the era is not in the packet.

transmit_timestamp_fraction.description: Time at the server when the response left for the client, in NTP timestamp format.
transmit_timestamp_fraction.note: The Fraction half of the NTP timestamp format (section 6, Figure 3), scaled by 2^-32, which is exact. Add it to the seconds field.
